signatures.object: Per-app hierarchical memory: page nodes (defined by their sub-task lists), sub-task edges (parameterised action sequences), tasks (sequences of node/sub-task pairs)
signatures.information: Simplified HTML screen representation, user instruction, LLM outputs of Explore/Select/Derive (GPT-4-turbo) and slot-filling (GPT-3.5); offline random-explorer and trace-monitor screens; no outcome oracle
signatures.operation: Explore->Select->Derive on a cache miss; store the completed task; Recall replays the stored sub-task sequence with slot-filling, attribute-based action adaptation, and a one-shot in-context adaptation fallback
signatures.output: Reusable task/sub-task/action records with generalised UI attributes and parameter placeholders
signatures.conditions: Android apps with text-extractable layouts; repeated tasks and overlapping sub-tasks
signatures.feedback: Execution errors (invalid index, no screen change, loops) and optional human repair
signatures.selection_rule: Store when Select returns Finish; node dedup by sub-task requirements plus cosine similarity; no measured admission test
signatures.persistence: Server-side per-app graph reused across sessions
signatures.later_use: Instruction -> high-level task match -> memory replay, sub-task reuse in other tasks, few-shot example on fallback
signatures.claimed_effect: Warm-start latency -62.5%, cost -68.8% vs same-prompt Derive-only baseline; cold-start success 82.7% vs AutoDroid 74.7 / AppAgent 67.4
signatures.failure_boundary: UI changes, ambiguous attributes, image-only screens (Flutter/web/maps), crucial irreversible actions during repair

signatures.object: Executed path corrected by rule-based self-feedback or a human, then written to memory
signatures.information: Rule-detected error messages appended to next prompt; human edits sub-task list, selected sub-task/parameters, or demonstrated actions
signatures.operation: Within-episode self-correction (not retained) and human repair (retained in the stored path / example)
signatures.output: Repaired task path stored for recall

gap.author_gap: LLM task automators are unreliable (non-deterministic) and costly in time and money on repeated tasks; demonstration/macro approaches need human demos or fail to generalise actions.
gap.checked_gap: Real and measurable for repetitive mobile tasks (cost/latency, repeat-run variability); the paper's own accuracy results show memory lowers cost rather than improving autonomous accuracy.
gap.lineage: API assistants / programming-by-demonstration -> LLM agents without memory (AutoDroid, AppAgent) -> LLM agent with sub-task-level reusable memory; macro mining (Li & Riva, Toyama random explorer, Huang et al.)
gap.closest_adjacent: AutoDroid and AppAgent (empirical baselines), macro-mining work (discussed), LLM response caching; agent-memory work such as ExpeL/Voyager-style stores is not discussed
gap.residue: Repeated-task cost and latency; error repetition across overlapping sub-tasks
gap.stakes: Over two minutes and about one dollar per task as stated anecdotally
gap.method_response: Sub-task-level memory with parameter generalisation, adaptive recall and human repair
gap.remaining_gap: No autonomous accuracy gain from memory, no invalidation under UI change, generalisation to unseen task types untested, Android text-layout only
unresolved: AutoDroid's exploration-derived app knowledge and generic agent-memory neighbours are not available in the pinned materials; novelty of 'first caching' is taken from the authors.

assessment.evidence_level_note: The retained memory measurably improves later runs in latency/cost on sibling instructions of the same task (and anecdotally across tasks sharing sub-tasks). It does not improve autonomous accuracy (Table 1 warm 82.16% vs cold 82.7%); the 98.75% warm accuracy includes stored human repairs. Retained improvement is therefore efficiency, not autonomous capability.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On the authors' repeated-task set, a stored per-app sub-task memory lets sibling instructions run with far fewer LLM calls (latency -62.5%, cost -68.8% vs a same-prompt Derive-only baseline) while autonomous success stays at cold-start level (~82%); near-perfect recall (98.75%) holds only after human repair is stored (author-reported, single runs).
unresolved: Autonomous accuracy gain from memory not shown.
Generalisation to unseen task types and under app updates untested.

G.reason: Repeated-task cost/latency and run-to-run inconsistency are concrete (motivation anecdotal: >2 min, >$1 per task), and AutoDroid/AppAgent are run as baselines. But the novelty claim ("first to explore caching" in LLM task automators) is not differentiated from AutoDroid's exploration-built app memory, agent-memory/workflow-reuse neighbours are absent, and the reliability half of the stated gap is not what the memory addresses (warm 82.16% vs cold 82.7%). E.holdout.reason: Headline numbers rest on privileged signals: Table 1 successes allow up to three extra attempts after evaluator-identified errors (A2: oracle retry -> E.holdout), and the 98.75% warm accuracy uses cold-start failures repaired by the authors and stored. Warm tests are the identical task (comparison, opus/O01) or a sibling instruction of the same task (ablation); evaluation apps were pre-explored (89.65% of pages). Cross-task reuse is anecdotal. Not 0: construction and scored instructions differ and the efficiency claim matches its stated repeated-task scope.

E.statistics.reason: Denominators (185 tasks, 80 tasks, 327 actions) and failures given; one run per task, no intervals or seeds; nondeterminism acknowledged; tests only in the user study (A2 ladder level 1).

Not 4: the §7.2 comparison is conditioned on 77 jointly successful tasks; human-repair effort and retries are not costed; long-run amortisation is projected.

shared_error_corrections.reason: Both seats kept the manifest's pre-v3 title in paper.title (each noted the discrepancy). The pinned v3 material is authoritative for the title; the manifest title is preserved as paper.manifest_title. Identity (ID, version, sha256) unchanged.

aggregate_review.initial_judgment_before_seat_scores: Read abstract, §3–§5, §7 (Tables 1–2) first. Memory of page nodes/sub-tasks/parameterised actions is stored after a run and replayed. Table 1 (no HITL): cold 82.7% vs warm 82.16% on the same task, so memory does not raise autonomous accuracy. Ablation: 98.75% warm on sibling instructions after authors repaired cold-start failures (§7.3.2 attributes the rise to user correction). Real gain = latency -62.5% / cost -68.8% on repeated tasks.
aggregate_review.integrity_checks: Both seats on 2312.03003v3, material sha256 82268715 matches manifest; input_hash/rubric hash identical; seat hashes equal conflicts.json; all quotes verified; C25/C03 parents valid; son55 duplicated a main card (resolved). Title discrepancy handled as a shared correction.
aggregate_review.core_claim_check: son55 hint confirmed in the original: warm 82.16% is not above cold 82.7% (Table 1; one extra recall failure) and the abstract's 98.75% includes stored human repair (§7.3.1 procedure, §7.3.2 explanation). Claim scoped to efficiency on repeated tasks.
aggregate_review.retention_check: Failure denominators: 185 tasks (Table 1) and 80 tasks (ablation), single runs. Selection vs test: memory built on the identical task or its sibling instruction; apps pre-explored. Budget/privileged: evaluator-gated retries (all systems), human repair (ablation, MobileGPT only benefits via memory), cost comparison on 77 jointly successful tasks. "Retained" holds for efficiency, not for an autonomous accuracy improvement.
